title: HINT for Software Engineers — code follows the spec
metaDescription: Keep architecture, contracts and failure rules beside code so every coding agent sees the constraints that apply before making a change.
h1: Your coding agent writes fast. HINT keeps it inside your architecture.
intro: HINT keeps plain-text engineering decisions beside the code they govern. Your agent reads only the relevant notes before it changes a file, so old constraints survive new sessions and new tools.

situations.before: A refactor quietly breaks an interface used by another language.
situations.after: The contract travels with the file
situations.body: The TypeScript renderer reads the exact shape declared by the Python compressor instead of guessing field names.

situations.before: A familiar pattern is applied where the repository deliberately forbids it.
situations.body: Architecture choices and rejected alternatives appear before implementation, while they can still change the approach.

situations.before: A happy-path patch ships without the errors and checks the system expects.
situations.after: Failure behavior is part of the task
situations.body: Error contracts, required flows and verification criteria arrive in the same scoped context as the code.

example.intro: The Pied Piper demo connects a Python compression stage to a TypeScript report renderer.
lines: The incoming message is the `CompressionResult` emitted by the compression engine.
A validated `CompressionResult` mirroring the compressor output.
example.after: It mirrors the upstream field names, follows the declared score formula, and reports any missing decision instead of inventing an interface.
example.compiled:
<function_contract name="renderReport">
  Read the upstream CompressionResult exactly.
  Compute the score with the declared formula.
  Return the specified report layout.
</function_contract>

never: Invent an API, field or dependency that the repository does not declare.
Replace a settled architectural decision with a generic preference.
Report success when required error paths or tests are missing.
disclaimer: HINT supplies project context; it does not prove that generated code is correct. Normal review, tests and security controls still apply.

faq.a: No. It keeps the durable decisions an agent needs next to the paths they govern and links to longer sources when needed.

faq.q: Does it work with an existing codebase?
faq.a: Yes. Add small `.hint` files gradually; `hint extract` can draft structural starting points where a language adapter exists.

faq.q: Is a model used to retrieve the rules?
faq.a: No. Scoped lookup and local search are deterministic and run without a network call.

keywordDescriptions.decision: Records a settled engineering choice and why it was made.
keywordDescriptions.invariant: States a property every change must preserve.
keywordDescriptions.entity: Defines a domain object and its role.
keywordDescriptions.field: Describes one field, including its type and constraints.
keywordDescriptions.func: Specifies a function's inputs, output and behavior.
keywordDescriptions.flow: Sets an ordered sequence that implementation must follow.
keywordDescriptions.error: Names a failure condition and its required response.
keywordDescriptions.test: Lists observable cases that prove the contract.
